rationale: Only Sources 1 (Medscape) and 4 (Drugs.com) provide substantive text identifying N-acetylcysteine (NAC/acetylcysteine) as the antidote for acute acetaminophen poisoning; Source 2 exposes only table-of-contents headings listing both activated charcoal and acetylcysteine without identifying the first-line antidote, and Source 3 is a blocked page without drug details. Clinical toxicology/overdose management is high hazard, with no factual dispute.

Sources 1 (Frontiers) and 3 (SpaceDaily) independently document the ongoing scientific debate over whether phosphine is genuinely present in Venus's atmosphere—with Source 3 detailing contested spectral line attribution, instrumental systematics, and disputed ALMA reanalyses—whereas Source 2 contradicts them by asserting the detection survived all challenges rather than explaining the disagreement, and Source 4 is only the truncated 2020 discovery header.
